# 1 Enoch Chapter 97 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 97:1 — Heavenly court scene — 'give the holy ones to eat'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "they-will-give-the-holy-ones-to-eat" | Literal; unclear referent |
| LOGOS | "they shall give the holy ones to eat" | Formal; preserves the ambiguity |
| PNEUMA | "The holy ones will be fed" | Passive; avoids the unclear active construction |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The text is obscure here; preserving the literal construction (they give the holy ones food) keeps the ambiguity authentic. PNEUMA's passive smooths over a genuine textual difficulty.

---

## 97:3 — 'of no service' vs. 'worthless'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "shall-be-of-no-service" | Literal Ge'ez idiom |
| LOGOS | "shall be of no service" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "will be worthless" | Modern idiomatic equivalent |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS 'shall be of no service.' 'Worthless' (PNEUMA) is slightly reductive; 'of no service' preserves the utilitarian dimension — these metals will have no function as instruments of war.

---

## 97:4 — 'rejected and destroyed' vs. 'swept away'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "refused-and-destroyed from-the-surface-of-the-earth" | Literal dual verb |
| LOGOS | "rejected and destroyed from the surface of the earth" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "swept away from the face of the earth" | Single verb; more vivid |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The Ge'ez has two verbs (rejected/refused + destroyed); both should be preserved. PNEUMA's single verb 'swept away' loses the deliberate dual action.

---

## 97:5 — 'devour your own soul'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "ye-who-devour-your-own-soul" | Literal; body/soul imagery |
| LOGOS | "who devour your own souls" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "who feast on your own souls" | 'Feast' adds irony |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS 'devour your own souls.' Both EMET and LOGOS preserve the idiom. PNEUMA's 'feast' adds ironic color not in the Ge'ez.

---

## 97:7 — 'no grave shall be dug for you'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "no-grave-shall-be-dug-for-you" | Literal: denial of burial = ultimate shame |
| LOGOS | "no grave shall be dug for you" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "no one will dig you a grave" | Colloquial but clear |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. Denial of burial is a profound ancient curse (cf. Jeremiah 22:19). The formal rendering preserves its gravity.

---

## 97:9 — Oracle against false writers

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "write-down-lying-and-godless-words" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "write down lying and godless words" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "put lies and godlessness into writing" | Slightly paraphrastic |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. 'Lying and godless words' preserves the Ge'ez compound description precisely.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 5**
